sentences.text: Dakotasuchus is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian, a group of crocodile relatives, belonging to the family Goniopholididae.
The animal featured twenty pairs of bony scutes, which are small, armor-like plates, running down the midline of its back.
Its short, broad shoulder blades suggest it possessed stout, powerful forelimbs and may have had terrestrial habits.
M. G. Mehl estimated the complete length of the type individual to be between 3 and 4 meters.
In 2017, additional fossils including a coracoid, scutes, a dorsal vertebra, and postcranial bones were found in the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah.
Fossils of Dakotasuchus were found in the Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Dakota Sandstone in Kansas.
The type specimen was discovered in an iron-cemented sandstone concretion near Salina.
The type species, D. kingi, was named in honor of Professor King, a former dean of Kansas Wesleyan University.
Robert Carroll assigned Dakotasuchus to the family Goniopholididae in 1988.
Dakotasuchus is classified within the family Pholidosauridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Pholidosauridae as the parent group for Dakotasuchus.
Dakotasuchus lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
